## Objective
- Practice running a benchmark drill to evaluate model performance on a standard dataset **(2026-08-11, https://github.com/benchmark-drill/guide)**  

## Setup
- Install required tools: Python 3.10+ and `pip install -r requirements.txt` **(2026-08-11, https://github.com/benchmark-drill/requirements)**  
- Download sample dataset (e.g., `wiki-text-20k`) from the provided URL **(2026-08-11, https://github.com/benchmark-drill/datasets)**  

## Execution Steps
- Run the benchmark script: `python run_benchmark.py --dataset wiki-text-20k --model gpt2` **(2026-08-11, https://github.com/benchmark-drill/scripts)**  
- Record elapsed time and accuracy metrics displayed in console **(2026-08-11, same source)**  

## Verification Checks
- Confirm `results.json` exists and contains expected keys (`latency`, `perplexity`) **(2026-08-11, https://github.com/benchmark-drill/validation)**  
- Compare computed perplexity against baseline (> 20 % improvement required) **(2026-08-11, same source)**  

## Common Failure Modes
- **Insufficient memory** – script crashes with “CUDA out of memory”; reduce batch size or run on CPU **(2026-08-11, https://github.com/benchmark-drill/troubleshooting)**  
- **Dataset download failure** – HTTP 404 or timeout; verify URL accessibility and internet connection **(2026-08-11, same source)**  
- **Version mismatch** – Python or library versions older than required cause import errors; ensure environment matches `requirements.txt` **(2026-08-11, same source)**  

## Tool Guidance
- Use `time` command or `timeit` for precise runtime measurement **(2026-08-11, https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html)**  
- For reproducible runs, set `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` and fix random seeds **(2026-08-11, same source)**
